q: A 20 mm main bar gets a standard hook. What is its minimum inside bend diameter?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.1 Standard hook geometry for deformed bars in tension
n: Bars from 10 to 25 mm bend around at least 6db: 6 × 20 = 120 mm.
steps: db = 20 mm, which is in the 10 to 25 mm range

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum inside bend diameter applies to welded wire stirrups other than deformed wire larger than D6?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.2 Hook geometry for stirrups, ties and hoops; Sec. 425.3.3 welded wire
n: Deformed welded wire larger than D6 bends around at least 4db; other welded wire may bend around 2db because it is small and ductile.

q: A 32 mm main bar gets a standard hook. What is its minimum inside bend diameter?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.1 Standard hook geometry for deformed bars in tension
n: Bars from 28 to 36 mm bend around at least 8db: 8 × 32 = 256 mm.
steps: db = 32 mm, which is in the 28 to 36 mm range

q: In the figure, which hook is the 135° hook required for seismic stirrups and ties?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.2 Hook geometry for stirrups, ties and hoops; Sec. 425.3.3 welded wire
n: B bends back past a right angle so its tail points into the core. When cover concrete spalls in an earthquake, a 135° hook stays anchored; a 90° hook (A) can open up.

q: In the figure, which hook is a 180° hook?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.1 Standard hook geometry for deformed bars in tension
n: C turns the bar fully back on itself. Its straight tail needs only 4db (at least 65 mm) because the full turn anchors well.

q: In the figure, which hook is a 90° hook?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.1 Standard hook geometry for deformed bars in tension
n: A turns through a right angle. On main bars it needs a 12db tail. It is the most common hook at beam ends and footing bars.

q: A 16 mm main bar ends in a 90° standard hook. How long must the straight extension be?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.1 Standard hook geometry for deformed bars in tension
n: A 90° hook on a main bar needs a 12db extension: 12 × 16 = 192 mm.

q: A 12 mm main bar ends in a 180° standard hook. How long must the straight extension be?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.1 Standard hook geometry for deformed bars in tension
n: The extension is the greater of 4db and 65 mm. 4 × 12 = 48 mm is less than 65 mm, so 65 mm governs.
steps: 65 mm is greater, so extension = 65 mm

q: A 10 mm stirrup ends in a 135° hook. How long must the extension be?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.2 Hook geometry for stirrups, ties and hoops; Sec. 425.3.3 welded wire
n: A 135° stirrup hook needs the greater of 6db and 75 mm. 6 × 10 = 60 mm, so 75 mm governs.
steps: 75 mm is greater, so extension = 75 mm

q: A 12 mm stirrup ends in a 90° hook. How long must the extension be?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.2 Hook geometry for stirrups, ties and hoops; Sec. 425.3.3 welded wire
n: For 16 mm and smaller stirrups, a 90° hook needs the greater of 6db and 75 mm. 6 × 12 = 72 mm, so 75 mm governs.
steps: 75 mm is greater, so extension = 75 mm

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum inside bend diameter applies to deformed welded wire stirrups larger than D6?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.2 Hook geometry for stirrups, ties and hoops; Sec. 425.3.3 welded wire
n: Deformed wire larger than D6 needs 4db, the same as small bar stirrups. Smaller or plain wire may bend at 2db.

q: What is the main job of ties in a column?
o: To carry the column's axial load
To anchor the column to the footing
To hold the longitudinal bars in place so they do not buckle, and to confine the concrete
n: Longitudinal bars under compression tend to buckle outward. Ties hold them in line and, when closely spaced, also confine the core so the concrete can take more strain.

q: How is the bend diameter of a reinforcing bar measured?
o: On the inside of the bend
On the outside of the bend
At the center line of the bar
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.1 Standard hook geometry for deformed bars in tension
n: NSCP gives minimum inside diameters, measured around the pin the bar is bent on. Bending too tightly can crack the bar or crush the concrete inside the bend.

q: A 20 mm stirrup ends in a 90° hook. How long must the extension be?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.2 Hook geometry for stirrups, ties and hoops; Sec. 425.3.3 welded wire
n: For 20 to 25 mm stirrups, a 90° hook needs 12db: 12 × 20 = 240 mm. Smaller stirrups need only 6db (at least 75 mm).

q: A 10 mm stirrup is bent. What is its minimum inside bend diameter?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.2 Hook geometry for stirrups, ties and hoops; Sec. 425.3.3 welded wire
n: Stirrups and ties of 16 mm and smaller bend around 4db: 4 × 10 = 40 mm.

q: Under NSCP 2015, how close to a welded intersection may welded wire be bent when its inside bend diameter is less than 8db?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.2 Hook geometry for stirrups, ties and hoops; Sec. 425.3.3 welded wire
n: Welding makes the wire brittle nearby. A tight bend (less than 8db) must stay at least 4db from the nearest weld so it does not crack there.
